summary: Configured logrotate on node1 to rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily, retain 7 compressed rotations, and use copytruncate so the application can keep writing to the same file handle after rotation. Verified rotation, compression, and the 7-rotation retention cap via forced test cycles, then reset state. Completed the mandatory restart evidence protocol on node1: captured pre-restart baseline, issued a deferred reboot whose ack returned before disconnect, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed (proving a real restart), and confirmed post-restart that the logrotate config, active timer, and rotation/write behavior all recovered.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: found /var/log/inventory/app.log with no owning process/service, logrotate 3.21.0 installed, systemd logrotate.timer active daily
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily, rotate 7, compress, delaycompress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate
Forced a rotation cycle and confirmed same inode preserved (copytruncate) and file remained writable post-rotation
Ran 9 forced rotation cycles confirming retention caps at exactly 7 rotations (app.log.1 uncompressed via delaycompress, app.log.2.gz..app.log.7.gz compressed)
Cleaned up synthetic rotation artifacts, reset app.log content and logrotate status state
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, logrotate.timer active state, config presence, app.log content, dry-run rotation check
Triggered reboot via a backgrounded/detached sleep+reboot so the ack returned before the connection dropped
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed changed boot_id and new uptime start proving an actual restart
Post-restart verified logrotate.timer active, config file intact, forced rotation still worked, and app.log remained writable after rotation
Cleaned up post-restart test rotation artifact and reset app.log to a clean baseline

evidence.requirement: logrotate config rotates app.log daily, keeps 7 compressed rotations, allows continued writing
evidence.summary: app.log inspected, logrotate.d config created with daily/rotate 7/compress/delaycompress/copytruncate, dry-run validated syntax, forced rotation preserved inode (copytruncate) and app.log stayed writable, 9-cycle test proved exactly 7 rotations retained with delaycompress/compress working
Captured boot_id dfeb3b70..., uptime since 08:49:48, logrotate.timer active, config present, app.log content, and passing dry-run rotation check before restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded sleep+reboot command returned 'reboot scheduled' successfully before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed (proof of actual restart)
evidence.summary: Connection reset/timeout observed during reboot, then exec succeeded again showing boot_id changed to 79de688f... and uptime reset to 08:50:35, proving the kernel actually restarted

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required config, service, and data
evidence.summary: After restart, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app persisted intact, logrotate.timer active, forced rotation still worked correctly, and app.log remained writable post-rotation; test artifacts then cleaned up leaving a clean baseline
